description: Clarify the in-game sound affordance so players understand sound is opt-in and browser-permission dependent.
steps: Use and consult miner-daily-task-runner before implementing; run ./init.sh and inspect the intro/HUD sound affordance before editing.
Inspect src/ui.tsx, src/styles.css, src/dom.ts, src/audio.ts, and UI tests for the existing Sound button, intro copy, and accessible labels.
Add concise player-facing copy or button state text that explains sound can be enabled intentionally, without crowding the HUD or mobile layout.
Ensure the affordance updates consistently when sound is enabled, disabled, blocked, or unavailable, while preserving current DOM IDs/classes consumed by the runtime.
Add or update tests that assert the sound control renders with accessible labeling and any new status text or helper output.
Run ./init.sh and perform a live smoke at desktop and narrow/mobile viewport sizes to confirm the sound guidance is visible, non-overlapping, and does not interfere with play.
acceptance: Players can tell from the intro/HUD that sound is optional and should be enabled through the Sound control or a trusted tap/click gesture.
The sound affordance remains readable on mobile-sized layouts and does not overlap critical fuel, hull, cargo, shop, or intro content.
Existing Sound button behavior, keyboard controls, intro flow, and live gameplay remain intact with no runtime exceptions.
Before marking complete, run ./test.sh plus canonical verification npm test, npm run typecheck, and npm run build.
